minor.issue: After a teleport the empty-castle slot is re-created at the source coordinates with slot_status='FREE'. A second POST with the same slot_id + a fresh idempotency_key therefore SUCCEEDS (swapping the castle back) instead of returning 409 TELEPORT_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE as the review request expected. Behavior is consistent (each swap costs 2000 Rubies, ledger stays balanced) but the review contract asks the slot to be considered unavailable at that id after use — please confirm design intent (allow perpetual swap-back vs mark slot exhausted / mint a new slot_id).

action_items: Design clarification: same slot_id + new idempotency_key currently succeeds after teleport (perpetual swap). Review request expected 409 TELEPORT_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE. If the current behavior is intended, update the review contract; otherwise mark the freshly-vacated slot with a new slot_id (or leave it non-FREE) so the same slot_id cannot be re-consumed. All Ruby ledger + persistence behavior is correct in either interpretation.

rca_of_issue: Discrepancy on 'same slot_id reused' expectation: teleport() sets the freshly-vacated PLAYER_SLOT doc back to slot_status='FREE' at the source coordinates (teleport.py L102). This is deliberate — the slot must remain as a bookable empty castle in the region. But because it keeps the SAME slot_id, a subsequent POST with that slot_id + a new idempotency_key passes the FREE+region filter and swaps the castle back to the source position (verified: from:[1596,618] → to:[1442,458], rubies 993999 → 991999). This costs 2000 Rubies each swap so the ledger is safe, but the review contract expects 409 TELEPORT_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE for 'slot no longer FREE at that id'. Two possible fixes if the intent is single-use: (a) mint a new slot_id when re-materializing the empty castle at the old coords (uuid4), or (b) tag the freshly-vacated slot with a cool-down field and add it to slot_q. Neither is applied in this run since the ledger/business flow is otherwise correct and the review might accept perpetual swap-back.
